description: The Dawn Framing Camera is a multispectral CCD imager in a refracting telescope. Each of the two identical cameras has a filter wheel with one clear filter and seven narrow-band filters, used both to map Vesta and Ceres and for optical navigation.
facility_description: Dawn is the NASA mission to the asteroids 4 Vesta and 1 Ceres; the Framing Camera is the German imaging contribution, flown as two identical units.
notes: Filter numbers F1-F8 in the PDS FC2 instrument catalog match Schröder et al.: F1 is the clear filter and F2-F8 are the narrow-band filters. The catalog peak of 700 nm for F1 is not the effective wavelength; Schröder et al. Table 3 lists F1 central wavelength 735 nm and effective wavelength 732 nm, and lists effective wavelengths for F2-F8 that match the catalog. ADS abstract pages returned HTTP 405, so no bibcode was copied. The Springer article page for 10.1007/s11214-011-9745-4 returned a client-challenge document; the DOI is taken from the PDS FC1 context page and from Crossref. The Schröder manuscript on arXiv is marked CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0. The band wavelengths quoted here are from the PDS instrument catalog, and the calibration-pipeline report archived with the PDS Dawn FC data (DA-FC-MPAE-RP-272, issue 2, revision b) had no copyright or restrictive-licence sentence in its extracted text. PDS citing pages say to cite the data product but do not give a fixed acknowledgement sentence. The NASA licence sentence is used because these are calibration and auxiliary descriptions from the NASA-led Dawn mission in the PDS. Images are digitized to 14 bits on a frame-transfer CCD; that is not a statement of photon versus energy weighting. The NASA licence page qualifies that sentence: it applies unless the data file is marked with a restrictive notice or license.

licence.terms: "There are no restrictions on the usage of these data."
